targets.title: Targets
targets.intro: A target is a server the box sends backups to over SSH, for example a storage box you rent or another Linux server. Each target gets its own key, and the box connects only to the server whose host key you confirmed.
targets.empty: Add the server your backups should go to.
targets.publicKeyHint: Add this line to the file .ssh/authorized_keys of the user on the server. The box signs in only with this key and stores no password.
targets.copyFailed: Select the key and copy it by hand.
targets.testPassed: The box signed in, opened the folder and wrote a test file.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: How the target is named in the Backup app
form.portHint: Usually 22; some storage providers use 23 for SSH
form.pathHint: Relative to the user's login folder, or from / on. Empty for the login folder. The test creates it if it is missing.

add.title: Add target
add.fingerprints: The server offered these host keys. Compare the fingerprint with the one your provider or the server's administrator shows you (on the server itself: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub). Save only if it matches: the box will connect to no other server for this target.
add.saved: {name} is saved. Add its public key on the server, then test the connection.

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.moved: The server or port changed, so the box needs the new server's host key confirmed.

hostKey.title: Check the host key of {name}
hostKey.intro: The server now offers another host key than the one you confirmed. That is expected after the server was reinstalled or moved; otherwise someone may be posing as it. Compare the new fingerprint with the one your provider shows before you accept it.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.text: The box forgets the target and its key. Remove the public key from the server's authorized_keys as well; backups already on the server stay there.

jobs.title: Box backups
jobs.intro: Folders of this box, backed up to a target outside it: an SFTP server or a second box. Each run first takes a ZFS snapshot, so the backup shows one moment. A versioned backup keeps as many versions as you set; a mirror keeps one plain copy.
jobs.empty: Add the first backup of shared folders and homes to a target.
jobs.noTargets: A backup needs a server to back up to. Add a target first.
jobs.name: Name
jobs.daysLabel: Last 14 days: {succeeded} without problems, {warning} with warnings, {failed} failed, {none} without a backup

jobForm.name: Name
jobForm.repositoryHint: Below the target's folder. The box creates the repository there with a new key, which it shows once.
jobForm.repositoryFixed: Backs up to {repository} on {target}. The target and the repository of a backup stay; for another one, add a new backup.
jobForm.existingKeyHint: The key the box showed when the repository was made, for example before a reinstall.
jobForm.sourcesHint: A shared folder or home on a pool, and a folder inside it, or nothing for all of it.
jobForm.cronHint: Five fields in the box's time zone: minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week. For example 30 2 * * 1-5.
jobForm.timeInvalid: Enter the time as hours and minutes, for example 02:00.
jobForm.retentionHint: After every successful backup the box removes older versions beyond these and frees their space. All 0 keeps every version.
jobForm.checkOn: Check the repository on a schedule
jobForm.checkHint: In the box's time zone. A failed check is reported to the administrators.
jobForm.checkReadPercent: Data to read back, in percent
jobForm.checkReadPercentHint: 0 checks only the structure; more reads that share of the data from the target each time.
jobForm.overdueHint: Empty: three times the interval, at least two days.
jobForm.excludesHint: One restic pattern per line, for example *.tmp or **/cache.
jobForm.kindVersionedHint: Encrypted in a restic repository, with as many versions as you set. Files come back through Restore.

key.title: Key of {name}
key.warning: This key opens the repository, and the box shows it only now. Without it nobody can restore from this repository, also not after a reinstall of the box. Store it outside the box, for example in a password manager or on paper.
key.copyManually: Select the key and copy it by hand.
key.stored: I stored the key outside the box
key.fileIntro: Pithyx backup key of the backup {name}, repository {repository} on {target}. Keep it secret.
key.warningAgain: This key opens the repository. Keep it outside the box and never share it.
key.stepUp: {twoFactor, select, true {The key opens every version of this backup. Confirm with your password and the code from your authenticator app.} other {The key opens every version of this backup. Confirm with your password.}}

deleteJob.title: Delete {name}?
deleteJob.text: The box forgets the backup, its runs and its key. The repository stays on the target; without the key nobody can read it.

activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: What runs now, what waits and every run so far.
activity.nothingRunning: Nothing is running. The next runs start on their schedule.
activity.unreadableTitle: {count, plural, one {# file not backed up} other {# files not backed up}}
activity.unreadableMore: {count, plural, one {and # more file} other {and # more files}}
activity.unreadableHint: The rest of the version is complete. Give the box read access to these files, or exclude them in the backup's settings.

overview.title: Overview
overview.empty: Add a backup of shared folders and homes to a server or a second box.

calendar.ran: {count, plural, one {# backup ran} other {# backups ran}}
calendar.failedRuns: {count, plural, one {# run failed} other {# runs failed}}
calendar.warningRuns: {count, plural, one {# with warnings} other {# with warnings}}

overview.unreadable: {count, plural, one {# file could not be read} other {# files could not be read}}

detail.overdueDefault: Three times the interval, at least two days

versions.empty: No version yet. The first backup makes one.
versions.title: Version of {time}

chart.title: Size per version
chart.label: {count, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}, the newest holds {size}

restore.title: Restore
restore.intro: Pick a backup and one of its versions, then files or folders. The box puts them back with their owners, permissions and times.
restore.noJobs: Restoring needs a box backup with at least one version.
restore.noVersions: This backup has no version yet. Its first run makes one.
restore.compared: Changes against the version before are marked
restore.files: Files and folders in the version
restore.name: Name
restore.empty: This folder is empty in this version.
restore.beside: Put next to the current one
restore.noneSelected: Select files or folders to restore
restore.selectedFiles: {count, plural, one {# selected} other {# selected}}, files {size}
restore.dialogTitle: {count, plural, one {Restore one entry} other {Restore # entries}}
restore.dialogIntro: From {name}, version of {time}. Folders that are already there are merged.

places.originalHint: Each entry goes back to its folder; missing folders above it are made again.
places.folderHint: Each entry goes into the folder you pick, under its name.

restore.folderHint: Empty for its top, for example Restored/2026
restore.conflict: When a file is already there

conflicts.keepBothHint: The restored file goes next to it, named after the version's time. A file with the same size and time as the one there is left out.
conflicts.overwriteHint: The restored file takes its place. A folder is never replaced; both are kept.
conflicts.skipHint: The file in place stays; the restored one is left out.

restore.doneCounts: Restored: {restored} put back, {replaced} replaced, {renamed} kept next to the current one, {skipped} left out.

pulls.title: Server backups
pulls.intro: Folders of Linux servers that this box pulls over SSH with rsync into a folder of a shared folder, keeping versions as ZFS snapshots. Nothing of Pithyx runs on the server.
pulls.empty: Add the first backup of a Linux server onto this box.
pulls.noTargets: A server backup needs a server to read from. Add a server first.

owners.server: Owners and permissions as on the server

servers.title: Servers
servers.intro: A server is a Linux machine whose folders the box pulls onto itself over SSH. Each server gets its own key, which may only read with rsync below one folder, and the box connects only to the server whose host key you confirmed.
servers.empty: Add the Linux server whose folders the box should back up.
servers.authorizedKeysHint: Add this line to the file .ssh/authorized_keys of the user on the server. With it the key can only read with rrsync below {path}: no shell, no writing, no forwarding. The server needs rsync and its helper rrsync, which current distributions install with rsync.
servers.testPassed: The box signed in and rsync listed the folder.

serverForm.pathHint: Absolute and without spaces, / for the whole server. The backups choose folders below it.
serverForm.userHint: To keep every file with its owners, sign in as root; the key stays read-only either way.

addServer.title: Add server
addServer.saved: {name} is saved. Add its line to authorized_keys on the server, then test the connection.

deleteServer.text: The box forgets the server and its key. Remove its line from the server's authorized_keys as well; the server backups already on this box stay.

pullForm.pathsHint: One path per line, starting with /, from the folder the server's key may read: with / there, for example /etc or /srv/www. Each lands in the folder on this box with that path.
pullForm.folderHint: The box makes this folder in the shared folder as a dataset of its own. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, no spaces.
pullForm.readable: Everyone who may open the shared folder can read the copied files. Choose one only administrators can open for a server with secrets.
pullForm.fixed: Pulls from {server} into {destination}. The server and the folder on this box stay; for others, add a new backup.
pullForm.delete: Remove what was removed on the server
pullForm.deleteHint: Off keeps files on this box that are gone on the server. The versions keep them either way.
pullForm.ownersServer: As on the server: user and group ids, permissions, ACLs and extended attributes
pullForm.ownersBox: Owned by the box, with the permissions of the shared folder
pullForm.excludesHint: One rsync pattern per line, for example *.tmp or /var/cache/.

deleteJobPull.text: The box forgets the backup and its runs. The folder {destination} with its versions stays unless you delete it too.
deleteJobPull.data: Also delete the folder and all its versions
deleteJobPull.dataHint: Deletes the dataset {dataset} with every snapshot. This cannot be undone.

chooser.title: What do you want to back up?

out.title: Back up folders of this box
out.text: Shared folders and homes go to a target outside this box.
out.point1: to an SFTP server or a second box
out.point2: encrypted with versions, or as a plain mirror

in.title: Back up a Linux server onto this box
in.text: The box pulls folders of a server over SSH and keeps them with versions on a pool.
in.point1: the server needs only SSH and rsync

mirrorForm.kindHint: One plain copy of the folders on the target, written with rsync over SSH. Each run brings it up to date; the files can be opened there directly.
mirrorForm.warning: A mirror keeps no versions and is not encrypted: a file changed, damaged or encrypted by malware on the box is changed on the target too at the next run. Needs rsync on the target; on a second box, use a user who may sign in over SSH.
mirrorForm.folderHint: Below the target's folder. The box creates it if it is missing; a copy already there is brought up to date.
mirrorForm.fixed: Mirrors into {repository} on {target}. Target and folder of a mirror stay; for another one, add a new mirror.
mirrorForm.delete: Delete on the target what was deleted here
mirrorForm.deleteHint: Off keeps files on the target that are gone on the box. On, a file deleted here by mistake is gone from the copy after the next run too.
mirrorForm.excludesHint: One rsync pattern per line, for example *.tmp or cache/.

deleteJobMirror.text: The box forgets the mirror and its runs. The copy stays on the target.
